convoLines.text: "Short version — Any regrets? The real kind, not the small stuff."
Quiet. "Yeah. I think everyone's carrying one of those."
"I regret the ordinary days I rushed through. All those Columbus, Ohio mornings I spent annoyed at small things. I'd pay anything for one annoyed morning now. — or so they tell me."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on your regrets."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"I don't actually want to belong somewhere. I want to make the System explain itself. I wish I could tell you why. I've asked myself that more times than you have."
"What if the monsters are drafts? Sketches it didn't finish? We're living in someone's sketchbook."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"The pantry's nearly bare. Come forage with me tomorrow — two of us can fill packs."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the murumuru patch past the treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"This one — Wild Strawberry. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"Caitlin owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can we talk?" Kurt sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Kurt has been stockpiling where nobody looks. "Take half. You've got the hands for it." (+4 wood, +4 fiber to the village stash.)
"I keep dreaming about rows of pods. Humming. Tell me I'm not the only one, anyway."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Since Caitlin died... I keep expecting to see Caitlin at the fire. Stupid."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"What's the worst thing you've done since the sky changed?"
No judgment in their face. "We're all doing math that doesn't add up. You're still here. That counts."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Thanks for listening. Most people change the subject."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Good day, huh? Almost feels normal."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on cheer."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Good times. What did you want to talk about?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "I dreamed Caitlin was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Nobody says Caitlin's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Maypop — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Kate?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.

"It's my aunt, Kate. Went in the Taking. She laughed like a screen door in a windstorm. Boring. Right. Some nights I swear I hear them before I sleep -- the pods, rows deep, humming. Then morning comes and I can't say whether it was real.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took Ines — Pattern Hunger, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"We'll see what the treeline brings. We always do."
"As I said — Still on what's been happening. No time to waste."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Never mind the sickness I'm fighting — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
"Okay." Bodhi looks down. "Okay, you got me. I wasn't a pharmacist. I was a pottery instructor. I keep my head down. Old habit. It kept me alive before; it keeps me alive now." Their voice is small.
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
Their tone levels out — courteous, careful, further away.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"You said there was something you needed to say, to someone, and now you can't. Found another way to say it yet?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "You want to know what I did in the raid? I stood down The Loud Beast at the treeline — it ran. Don't call it brave. Call it awake."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Gotta run. Literally. Bye!"
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Patience?"
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my older sister, Patience. Was taken. She raised me more than our mother did. Boring. That is what they wrote down. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"That again?" Bodhi sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind. It'll keep."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Bodhi rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Bodhi says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."

deathBeat: d10: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Caitlin Cruz is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d10: 🕯️ Caitlin Cruz is dead — dehydration. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
recoverHome: d11: That night, they bring Caitlin home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d10: ◈ SYSTEM: "Ooh. NEIGHBORS. You know what neighbors are for? STORYLINES. Go knock — worst case, it's CONTENT. Best case? The show gets BIGGER."
d10: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "The audience wants an encore. A trial, then — smaller this time, but televised." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.
d11: SYSTEM: Identification complete. You are 0.3% less lost.
d12: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 52. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d12: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
burialWindowSay: d10: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+5 integration)

d14: You say a few words for Caitlin. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d14: You bury Caitlin. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+2 trauma)
